original_test_intent: Verify the AMDGPU RAS PCIe path can inject correctable LCRC errors in both transmit and receive directions and that PCIe/AER handling records each event without losing or degrading the GPU link.
original_method: Record GPU/BDF/root-port/link/driver/tool/firmware identity and workloads; preserve AER/dmesg/lspci/link baseline; safely load ras_enable=1 and retain source UMC zero query with limited scope; resolve implicit target and Table3.13 semantics; run mode0 TX once, collect direction-specific tool/AER/driver/counter evidence and verify full link/device health; rebaseline; only then run mode1 RX once and repeat evidence/health checks; verify no device loss/hang/continuing AER and restore through owner recovery only.
manual_activity: PCIe/AMD platform owner approves BDF/root-port target, Table3.13 TX/RX semantics/order, AER oracle and recovery; agent may execute each approved phase once with health gate between them.
required_inputs: AMD GPU RAS Tool guide Table3.13 and direction-specific AER/status/counter expectations
Inter-phase reset/rebaseline/quiet-window requirements and correctable threshold policy
Approved PCIe/GPU reset, hot reset or reboot/OOB recovery plus ras_enable restoration
safety_requirements: Dedicated isolated SUT with live OOB/host recovery and no GPU workloads
Preserve AER/dmesg/link baselines; do not blanket-clear logs
Map implicit target before injection and never run TX/RX concurrently
After TX, require stable enumeration/link/GPU and approved rebaseline before RX
No retry or independent hot reset/reboot; stop on device loss, degraded width/speed, fatal escalation or hang
agent_execution_scope: Validate guide/tool/module, target topology and baseline
Observe one approved TX phase, collect evidence and enforce health gate, then one approved RX phase
Verify final PCIe/GPU/host health and restore settings
Do not select target/order, run phases concurrently, retry, hot-reset/reboot independently or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Approve BDF/root-port and Table3.13 direction mapping/order

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Partly useful but conflates severity classes and omits exact mode0 TX/mode1 RX, Table3.13 and separated attribution; tail100/lspci alone lacks AER status/counters and link parameters.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain module/source UMC precheck, then separately run `sudo amdgpuras -b 5 -s 1 -t 2 -m 0` and after a passed health/rebaseline gate `sudo amdgpuras -b 5 -s 1 -t 2 -m 1`; capture full AER/dmesg/lspci/link evidence per phase.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Block5, subtype1, type2, mode0 TX, mode1 RX, Table3.13, success/dmesg criteria, Common branch and30/30 minutes are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat TX and RX as two attributed subphases separated by an enumeration/link-health gate, not a back-to-back undifferentiated run.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact topology, severity/direction-specific AER oracle, phase isolation, rebaseline and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: One combined log window cannot prove both LCRC directions or identify which phase caused link degradation.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Even correctable AER can retrain/degrade a marginal link; the commands omit an explicit device and the source UMC baseline does not prove PCIe cleanliness.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row200 Wistron-GPU RAS-00015-V002: approve platform/BMC and implicit GPU UUID/OAM/BDF/root-port/link target, amdgpuras version/hash/license and Table3.13; confirm block5/subtype1/type2 mode0=LCRC TX and mode1=LCRC RX, direction-specific AER/status/counter oracle, inter-phase rebaseline/quiet-window and stop gate, source UMC-query coverage boundary, and PCIe/GPU reset/hot-reset/reboot/OOB no-retry recovery plus ras_enable restoration.

review_improvement: Retains both correctable LCRC directions while making them separately attributable and adding a mandatory health gate that prevents a damaged TX phase from being followed by RX.
independent_technical_reasoning: TX and RX LCRC faults exercise different ends/directions of the PCIe data link and must generate separately attributable AER evidence. Back-to-back execution without checking enumeration, width/speed and counters can hide which phase caused degradation. The injection omits device identity, and a UMC zero query covers another block, so topology and PCIe baseline are mandatory. Correctable classification does not eliminate host/link risk; device loss or fatal escalation stops the sequence and forbids retry.
